# ALMASim command-line reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_cli_reference.py from the command
definitions; edit those and rerun the script instead of this file. -->

`almasim` has 9 command groups and 5 single commands. Each
group's commands are listed with their arguments and options. Hidden
commands (kept for compatibility) are left out.

## `almasim metadata`

Query ALMA metadata from TAP and save normalized CSV results.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim metadata [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--source-name <str>`: Source-name substring filter.
* `--science-keyword <str>`: Science keyword(s) to include. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--scientific-category <str>`: Scientific category(ies) to include. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--band <int>`: ALMA band filter. Repeat for multiple values.
* `--antenna-arrays <str>`: Raw antenna_arrays substring filter.
* `--array-type <str>`: Array type(s): 12m, 7m, TP. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--array-configuration <str>`: Array configuration(s) like C-1, C-2. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--angular-resolution-min <float>`: Minimum angular resolution (arcsec).
* `--angular-resolution-max <float>`: Maximum angular resolution (arcsec).
* `--observation-date-start <str>`: Observation date start (ISO date).
* `--observation-date-end <str>`: Observation date end (ISO date).
* `--qa2-status <str>`: QA2 status values: Pass, Fail, SemiPass, T, F, X.
* `--obs-type <str>`: Observation type(s) to include. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--fov-min <float>`: Minimum FOV.
* `--fov-max <float>`: Maximum FOV.
* `--time-resolution-min <float>`: Minimum time resolution.
* `--time-resolution-max <float>`: Maximum time resolution.
* `--frequency-min <float>`: Minimum frequency.
* `--frequency-max <float>`: Maximum frequency.
* `--exclude-science-keyword <str>`: Science keyword(s) to exclude. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--exclude-scientific-category <str>`: Scientific category(ies) to exclude. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--exclude-source-name <str>`: Source-name substring(s) to exclude. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--exclude-obs-type <str>`: Observation type substring(s) to exclude. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--exclude-solar`: Exclude solar observations.
* `--cycle <int>`: ALMA cycle number(s). Cycle N maps to proposal_id prefix {2012+N}.
* `--project-code <str>`: Exact ALMA project code(s). Repeat for multiple or pass comma-separated values. Example: --project-code 2019.1.00001.S --project-code 2022.1.00333.S
* `--public-only / --include-proprietary`: Restrict to public data (default: public only).  [default: public-only]
* `--science-only / --include-non-science`: Restrict to science observations (default: science only).  [default: science-only]
* `--exclude-mosaic / --include-mosaic`: Exclude mosaic observations (default: excluded).  [default: exclude-mosaic]
* `--visible-column <str>`: Column(s) to include in output (ordered). Repeat this option per column.
* `--limit <int range>`: Maximum number of metadata rows to keep. Defaults to unlimited.  [x>=1]
* `--save-csv <path>`: Destination CSV for normalized metadata rows.
* `--save-products-csv <path>`: Optional destination CSV for the DataLink product rows of the queried member OUS UIDs, ready for `products download --products-csv`.
* `--product-member-limit <int range>`: How many queried member OUS UIDs to resolve into product rows. Defaults to unlimited.  [x>=1]
* `--count-executions`: Add n_executions: how many execution blocks observed each row's MOUS (its raw ASDMs in DataLink; one request per MOUS). Int.Time is the MOUS's total, which `simulation run` observes in that many blocks.
* `-y, --yes`: Skip confirmation prompt and start the query immediately.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim products`

Data product resolution and download commands.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim products [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `resolve`: Extract member_ous_uid values and resolve...
* `download`: Download ALMA products and optionally...
* `executions`: Add how many execution blocks observed...

### `almasim products resolve`

Extract member_ous_uid values and resolve ALMA DataLink products.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim products resolve [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--metadata-csv <path>`: Metadata CSV containing member_ous_uid rows.
* `--member-ous-uid <str>`: Direct member_ous_uid values. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--member-limit <int range>`: Max metadata member_ous_uid rows to read (default: unlimited).  [x>=1]
* `--save-member-ous-uid-list <path>`: Optional text file to write extracted member_ous_uid list (one per line).
* `--save-products-csv <path>`: Destination CSV for resolved DataLink products.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/resolved_products.csv]
* `--expand-archives`: List the files inside each member's product and auxiliary tars, one row per file, so single files can be picked with --include/--exclude (for example the '*.pbcor.fits' images). One more DataLink request per tar.
* `--layout <delivery|flat>`: Where --expand-archives puts the files it lists: 'delivery' in the folders of the ALMA delivery tree, <project>/science_goal.*/group.*/member.*/product/ (or calibration/, qa/, script/, log/), read from the start of one tar per member; 'flat' in --destination itself.  [default: delivery]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim products download`

Download ALMA products and optionally unpack/calibrate archive data.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim products download [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--products-csv <path>`: Previously resolved products CSV.
* `--metadata-csv <path>`: Metadata CSV containing member_ous_uid rows to resolve first.
* `--member-ous-uid <str>`: Direct member_ous_uid values. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--member-limit <int range>`: Max metadata member_ous_uid rows to read (default: unlimited).  [x>=1]
* `--product-filter <all|auxiliary|calibration|continuum|cubes|fits|other|qa_reports|raw|scripts|weblog>`: Subset of resolved products to download.  [default: all]
* `--expand-archives`: List the files inside each member's product and auxiliary tars, one row per file, so single files can be picked with --include/--exclude (for example the '*.pbcor.fits' images). One more DataLink request per tar. Runs after --product-filter, on the selected tars only.
* `--layout <delivery|flat>`: Where --expand-archives puts the files it lists: 'delivery' in the folders of the ALMA delivery tree, <project>/science_goal.*/group.*/member.*/product/ (or calibration/, qa/, script/, log/), read from the start of one tar per member; 'flat' in --destination itself.  [default: delivery]
* `--include <str>`: Download only files whose name matches this glob, for example '*.pbcor.fits'. Repeat or pass comma-separated globs; a file matching any of them is kept.
* `--exclude <str>`: Skip files whose name matches this glob. Repeat or pass comma-separated globs.
* `--skip-qa0-semipass`: Skip raw ASDMs whose execution block is QA0 SemiPass, read from the <eb>.qa0_report.pdf in the member's extracted auxiliary delivery. ALMA never delivers calibration for these, so they can never be calibrated. Download and extract the auxiliary products first; a raw product without a readable report is kept.
* `--qa0-report-root <path>`: Root holding the extracted auxiliary deliveries (<project>/science_goal.*/group.*/member.*/qa/). Defaults to --destination.
* `--save-products-csv <path>`: Save resolved products CSV before download.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/resolved_products.csv]
* `--destination <path>`: Directory for downloaded files.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/downloads]
* `--max-parallel <int range>`: Max concurrent downloads across ALMA mirrors; capped at 30 (10 per mirror).  [default: 3; x>=1]
* `--extract-tar`: Extract downloaded tar/tgz archives.
* `--unpack-ms`: Import extracted ASDMs into raw MeasurementSets.
* `--generate-calibrated-visibilities`: Apply delivered calibrations and write calibrated MeasurementSets.
* `--archive-output-root <path>`: Root directory for archive_ms raw_ms/calibrated_ms products.
* `--casa-data-root <path>`: Optional CASA runtime data directory.
* `--skip-casa-data-update`: Do not auto-download CASA runtime data if missing.
* `--clean-intermediate-files`: Clean downloaded/intermediate raw files after calibrated outputs are created.
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 02:00:00]
* `--slurm-cores <int range>`: Cores per Slurm worker.  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 4GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Number of Slurm workers for post-processing. Pass 0 to spawn one worker per UID.  [default: 4; x>=0]
* `--overwrite-archive-outputs`: Overwrite existing raw/calibrated MS outputs.
* `--continue-on-error / --fail-fast`: Skip UIDs whose processing fails and carry on with the rest, then exit non-zero with a summary (default). --fail-fast aborts on the first failure.  [default: continue-on-error]
* `--keep-working-copies`: Keep each UID's working directory (raw MS copy plus caltables, about 1.8x the raw MS) after its calibrated output is written. By default it is removed.
* `-y, --yes`: Skip confirmation prompt and start download immediately.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim products executions`

Add how many execution blocks observed each row's MOUS (n_executions).

A row's Int.Time is its MOUS's total time on source; `simulation run`
observes it in n_executions blocks (without the column: blocks of at most
3000 s).

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim products executions [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--metadata-path <path>`: Metadata CSV (from 'almasim metadata') to add n_executions to.  [required]
* `--save-csv <path>`: Destination CSV; defaults to overwriting --metadata-path.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim simulation`

Run staged ALMASim simulation from a pre-queried metadata CSV.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim simulation [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--metadata-path <path>`: CSV file with pre-fetched ALMA metadata rows (from 'almasim metadata').  [required]
* `--row-idx <int range>`: Single metadata row index to simulate. Omit to simulate all rows.  [x>=0]
* `--project-name <str>`: Project name used in outputs.  [default: sim_demo]
* `--output-dir <path>`: Directory for simulation outputs.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/simulation]
* `--input <path>`: A sky-model cube, or a folder of them (an imaging run's: each spectral window's wsclean-cube-model.fits). Each cube is simulated with the metadata row of the observation its path names (an execution block, looked up in --products-csv, or a member OUS), on its own grid: size, pixel and frequency axis from its header. A file whose path names no observation is used for the chosen rows.
* `--products-csv <path>`: Resolved products (almasim products resolve) that map execution blocks to observations, for --input (default: the *products*.csv files next to --metadata-path).
* `--main-dir <path>`: Path to ALMASim data directory (defaults to src/almasim).  [default: <repo>/src/almasim]
* `--source-type <point|gaussian|diffuse|galaxy-zoo|molecular|hubble-100|external-components|external-fits-cube|external-fits-image>`: Sky model family (the external ones take their cube from --input).  [default: point]
* `--n-pix <int range>`: Spatial cube size (default 128; an --input cube sets its own).  [x>=1]
* `--n-channels <int range>`: Channel count (default 32; an --input cube sets its own).  [x>=1]
* `--n-lines <int range>`: Number of spectral lines to inject. Omit to use metadata default.  [x>=1]
* `--seed <int>`: Base random seed for reproducible simulations. When running multiple simulations, each run uses seed + run_index.
* `--simulations-per-row <int range>`: How many simulations to run for each selected metadata row.  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--imaging-algorithm <legacy>`: Channel imaging algorithm.  [default: legacy]
* `--robust <float>`: Robust weighting parameter for imaging.  [default: 0.0]
* `--instrument-geometry <legacy|planner>`: Beam, field of view and cell: legacy (the metadata FOV, beam / 5) or planner (the imaging planner's: the primary beam's FOV, beam / 8).  [default: legacy]
* `--background-mode <none|blank_field_dsfg|dusty_diffuse|combined>`: An astrophysical background added to the sky: blank_field_dsfg (faint dusty galaxies), dusty_diffuse (a smooth dusty field), combined (both) or none.  [default: none]
* `--background-level <float range>`: Strength of the --background-mode background, relative to the continuum sensitivity (default 1; 0 adds none).  [x>=0.0]
* `--background-seed <int>`: Random seed for background sky generation.
* `--inject-serendipitous`: Add a few random serendipitous sources around the target.
* `--save-mode <memory|npz|h5|fits>`: Output save mode.  [default: memory]
* `--persist-standard-outputs`: Persist standard outputs in addition to ML shard.
* `--ml-shard-path <path>`: Destination HDF5 shard path.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/ddrm_training_sample.h5]
* `--ms-export`: Also write each run's MeasurementSet, <project-name>_<run>.ms in --output-dir (in the run's own folder when there are several runs and products are kept), with any --save-mode: Stokes I in both hands, with the noise model's noise and WEIGHT. Needs casatools or python-casacore.
* `--casa-data-root <path>`: CASA runtime data for writing the MS with casatools (default <output-dir>/.casa-data, downloaded once when missing). python-casacore alone needs none.
* `--backend <sync|local>`: How the channels are imaged: sync, one after another in one process; local, in parallel worker processes on this node (--n-workers).  [default: sync]
* `--n-workers <int range>`: Worker processes for --backend local; give the job as many CPUs.  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--kaggle-token <path>`: Path to a Kaggle credentials file (JSON with username/key, e.g. kaggle.json or access_token) or the directory containing it, used to download morphology images for the galaxy-zoo / hubble-100 source types. Defaults to the standard Kaggle locations if omitted.
* `--noise-model, --corruptions <str>`: What the visibilities carry besides white thermal noise: a released noise model ('alma', the newest version, or 'alma@1': radiometer noise following ALMA's Tsys, correlated channels, antenna noise ripple and, on bright sources, the gain, atmospheric phase and baseline errors calibration leaves, as measured on real calibrated data; 'none'), a JSON object or a JSON file of a noise model. 'almasim noise show' lists the models.
* `--noise-only <str>`: Apply only these components of the noise model (comma-separated, e.g. 'radiometer,channel_correlation'); 'almasim noise show' lists them.
* `--noise-without <str>`: Apply the noise model without these components (comma-separated).
* `--executions <int range>`: How many of the MOUS's execution blocks to simulate (default: all). A row's Int.Time is the MOUS's total time on source; it is observed in blocks (the row's n_executions, else blocks of at most 3000 s), each a track near transit on its own day. 1 gives a single execution block.  [x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim visibilities extract`

Extract ALMA archive tarballs as a standalone step.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim visibilities extract [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--source-root <path>`: Directory containing downloaded archive files.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/downloads]
* `--destination <path>`: Extraction destination (defaults to --source-root).
* `--recursive / --no-recursive`: Recursively search --source-root for .tar/.tgz archives.  [default: recursive]
* `--delete-archives`: Delete each archive after successful extraction.
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 01:00:00]
* `--slurm-cores <int range>`: Cores per Slurm worker.  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 4GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Number of Slurm workers. Pass 0 to spawn one worker per archive.  [default: 4; x>=0]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--skip-existing`: Skip archives that have already been extracted (detected via a .done marker file).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim visibilities calibrate`

Create calibrated MeasurementSets as a standalone step.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim visibilities calibrate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--input-root <path>`: ALMA delivery root containing calibration products.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/downloads]
* `--raw-ms-root <path>`: Directory containing raw MeasurementSets.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/downloads/archive_ms/raw_ms]
* `--output-dir, --output-root <path>`: Directory where calibrated MeasurementSets are written.  [default: ~/almasim_outputs/downloads/archive_ms/calibrated_ms]
* `--asdm-uid <str>`: Optional UID(s) to calibrate. Repeat or pass comma-separated values.
* `--casa-data-root <path>`: Optional CASA runtime data directory.
* `--skip-casa-data-update`: Do not auto-download CASA runtime data if missing.
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 02:00:00]
* `--slurm-cores <int range>`: Cores per Slurm worker.  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 4GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Number of Slurm workers for post-processing. Pass 0 to spawn one worker per UID.  [default: 4; x>=0]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--overwrite-outputs`: Overwrite existing calibrated MS outputs.
* `--clean-intermediate-files`: Remove intermediate raw and working files after successful calibration.
* `--continue-on-error / --fail-fast`: Skip UIDs whose processing fails and carry on with the rest, then exit non-zero with a summary (default). --fail-fast aborts on the first failure.  [default: continue-on-error]
* `--keep-working-copies`: Keep each UID's working directory (raw MS copy plus caltables, about 1.8x the raw MS) after its calibrated output is written. By default it is removed.
* `--organize-delivery / --no-organize-delivery`: Link each calibrated MS into its member folder of the ALMA delivery tree (<project>/science_goal.*/group.*/member.*/calibrated/) and write ous_index.csv at the root of the tree. The tree is --input-root.  [default: organize-delivery]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim visibilities flag-summary`

Summarise flagging and visibility properties per MS, field and spectral window.

For each (field, SPW): intents, channels, correlations, scans, antennas,
time range and time on source, rows and visibilities flagged, median and
largest unflagged weight, and unflagged rows above --max-weight. Reads only
FLAG, FLAG_ROW, WEIGHT and the scalar columns, never DATA. An MS that cannot
be read is listed in ``<output>.failed.tsv`` and the exit status is 1.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim visibilities flag-summary [OPTIONS] {inputs}...
```

**Arguments**:

* `inputs...`: MeasurementSet(s) to summarise, or folders searched with --pattern. Several may be given.  [required]

**Options**:

* `-o, --output <path>`: CSV to write, one row per (MS, field, SPW).  [default: flag_summary.csv]
* `--pattern <str>`: Glob for the MeasurementSets inside a folder.  [default: *.ms.split.cal]
* `--max-weight <float>`: Unflagged rows with a WEIGHT above this count as high_weight_rows.  [default: 10000.0]
* `--require-done-marker / --no-require-done-marker`: In a folder, skip an MS whose <ms>.done calibration marker is missing. Only applies when the folder holds at least one such marker. MSs named directly are always summarised.  [default: require-done-marker]
* `--fail-fast`: Abort on the first MS that cannot be read (default: record it and continue).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim predict`

Predict visibilities from one MS or a folder of MSs.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim predict [OPTIONS] {input_ms_or_folder} {output_directory}
```

**Arguments**:

* `input_ms_or_folder`: Single MS directory or folder of MSs  [required]
* `output_directory`: Directory containing model FITS products  [required]

**Options**:

* `--use-slurm / --no-use-slurm`: Whether or not to use slurm or not  [default: use-slurm]
* `--num-cores <int range>`: Number of cores per predict task  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--max-cores-per-node <int range>`: Cores per node, for the Slurm workers' resource accounting.  [default: 95; x>=1]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 02:00:00]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 16GB]
* `--slurm-workers, --slurm-n-jobs <int range>`: Number of Slurm workers (jobs).  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--scheduler-interface <str>`: Scheduler/worker network interface (e.g. ib0, eth0).
* `--task-timeout <float range>`: Timeout in seconds for each worker-side command.  [default: 3600; x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim image compute-parameters`

Derive per-spectral-window imaging geometry for every MS in a folder.

An MS that cannot be read (a truncated table, say) is reported and listed
in ``<output>.failed.tsv`` instead of aborting the whole scan; the command
then exits with status 1 once every MS has been attempted.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim image compute-parameters [OPTIONS] [archive_folder] [output_metadata_file]
```

**Arguments**:

* `archive_folder`: Processed MSs folder (default: current directory)  [default: .]
* `output_metadata_file`: Parameters CSV file (default: imaging_parameters.csv)  [default: imaging_parameters.csv]

**Options**:

* `--pattern <str>`: Glob for the MeasurementSets inside the folder.  [default: *.cal]
* `--science-only / --all-spws`: One row per spectral window and per field observed with the selected intent (OBSERVE_TARGET by default). --all-spws gives a row per field, calibrators included. Only (window, field) pairs with visibilities are listed.  [default: science-only]
* `--intent <str>`: Scan intent selecting the fields, e.g. CALIBRATE_PHASE#ON_SOURCE, or CALIBRATE_PHASE for any sub-intent. Repeat for several. Default: OBSERVE_TARGET. Not with --all-spws.
* `--require-done-marker / --no-require-done-marker`: Skip an MS whose <ms>.done calibration marker is missing. Only applies when the folder holds at least one such marker, so plain folders still work.  [default: require-done-marker]
* `--fail-fast`: Abort on the first MS that cannot be read (default: record it and continue).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim image image-from-ms`

Image every (MS, spectral window) row of a parameter CSV with WSClean.

Each task leaves ``SPW-<n>.done`` or ``SPW-<n>.failed`` (with the error and
the log path) next to its output directory, and ``SPW-<n>.log`` with the
full WSClean output. A rerun skips the tasks with a ``.done`` marker and
retries the rest, so an interrupted batch can simply be resubmitted.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim image image-from-ms [OPTIONS] {imaging_parameters} {output_directory}
```

**Arguments**:

* `imaging_parameters`: Imaging parameter file  [required]
* `output_directory`: Output directory path  [required]

**Options**:

* `--fov-fraction <float range>`: Fraction of the FOV to image  [default: 1.5; x>=1e-06]
* `--beam-sampling <float range>`: Number of pixels to use to sample the synthetized beam. Could be fractional.  [default: 8; x>=1e-06]
* `--min-beams-across <float range>`: Make every image at least this many synthesized beams wide, whatever --fov-fraction gives (default 32; 0: no minimum).  [default: 32.0; x>=0.0]
* `--multiscale / --no-multiscale`: Clean with WSClean's multi-scale algorithm (-multiscale) for extended emission. Off by default: it can diverge on bright sources in small images.  [default: no-multiscale]
* `--num-cores <int range>`: Number of cores per imaging task  [default: 10; x>=1]
* `--max-cores-per-node <int range>`: Cores per node, for the Slurm workers' resource accounting.  [default: 95; x>=1]
* `--wsclean-bin <str>`: Path or executable name of the WSClean binary the workers run.  [default: wsclean]
* `--auto-threshold <float range>`: Stop cleaning when the residual peak drops below this many sigma of the residual noise (WSClean -auto-threshold; default 1, inside the --auto-mask mask). 0 disables it and cleaning runs to -niter.  [default: 1.0; x>=0.0]
* `--auto-mask <float range>`: WSClean -auto-mask level in sigma (default 3): clean to this level everywhere, then only inside the mask it found down to --auto-threshold. Must be above --auto-threshold; 0 disables masking.  [default: 3.0; x>=0.0]
* `--task-memory-gb <float range>`: Absolute memory limit per WSClean task in GB (WSClean -abs-mem). Use the worker's Slurm allocation divided by the tasks per node. 0 (default) falls back to -mem <num-cores/max-cores-per-node> percent of the node.  [default: 0.0; x>=0.0]
* `--single-window-ms / --no-single-window-ms`: Extract each task's spectral window (and target fields) into a per-task MS on the worker and image it with -no-reorder (default). WSClean 3.7's reordering reads out of bounds on multi-window ALMA sets and crashes about half the tasks; --no-single-window-ms images the original MS with -spws/-field instead.  [default: single-window-ms]
* `--task-retries <int range>`: Retry a task whose WSClean died by a signal (segfault) this many times before marking it failed. WSClean 3.7's multi-threaded reordering crashes non-deterministically on some inputs; a crash costs seconds.  [default: 3; x>=0]
* `--max-weight <float range>`: Leave visibility rows whose WEIGHT exceeds this out of the single-window MS (0 keeps every row). Calibrated ALMA rows the pipeline had flagged but that were never re-flagged carry WEIGHT ~1e5-1e8 with garbage amplitudes and would dominate the image; physical weights stay below ~1e3.  [default: 10000.0; x>=0.0]
* `--scratch-dir <path>`: Directory for WSClean's reordered visibilities (one sub-directory per task, removed afterwards). Default: the task's output directory.
* `--continuum-restart / --no-continuum-restart`: Clean the continuum in two passes, the second (-continue) from the true residual with a mask rebuilt at the true noise: the first pass's auto-mask, built while a bright source's sidelobes inflate the noise, misses its fainter parts (default; only with --single-window-ms, whose per-task copy gets MODEL_DATA).  [default: continuum-restart]
* `--update-model / --no-update-model`: Write the CLEAN model back into the MS MODEL_DATA column (WSClean -update-model-required). Off by default: concurrent spectral-window tasks would write the same MS and every calibrated MS would grow.  [default: no-update-model]
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: slurm]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 02:00:00]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 16GB]
* `--slurm-workers, --slurm-n-jobs <int range>`: Number of Slurm workers (jobs).  [default: 1; x>=1]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--scheduler-interface <str>`: Scheduler/worker network interface (e.g. ib0, eth0).
* `--task-timeout <float range>`: Timeout in seconds for each worker-side command.  [default: 3600; x>=1]
* `--skip-existing`: Also trust an existing wsclean-image.fits that has no .done marker (an output from before markers existed) and write its marker. Tasks with a marker are always skipped.
* `--overwrite-outputs`: Redo every task, including the ones with a .done marker.
* `--continue-on-error / --fail-fast`: Keep imaging the rest of the batch when a task fails (default); the failed tasks are listed at the end and the command exits 1. --fail-fast stops at the first failure.  [default: continue-on-error]
* `--continuum / --no-continuum`: Make the continuum image of every window (wsclean-image.fits; default). --no-continuum with --cube adds cubes next to existing continuum images.  [default: continuum]
* `--cube / --no-cube`: Also image every window as a spectral cube (WSClean -channels-out, the channel count chosen per window by --spectral-sampling, --velocity-resolution and --max-cube-gb), stacked into wsclean-cube-<product>.fits.  [default: no-cube]
* `--contsub / --no-contsub`: Also write the image cube continuum-subtracted (wsclean-cube-image.contsub.fits): a polynomial fitted along frequency per pixel, line channels found by 3-sigma clipping. Off by default. Needs --cube.  [default: no-contsub]
* `--selfcal <str>`: Self-calibrate each window with CASA gaincal before imaging, one round per comma-separated solution interval: inf (per scan), int (per integration) or <seconds>s for phase; ap:<interval> for amplitude and phase on top of the phase solution, e.g. 'inf,30s,ap:inf'. A round is kept only if the continuum S/N rises. Empty (default): off. Needs --continuum and --single-window-ms.
* `--selfcal-min-snr <float range>`: Skip self-calibration when the initial continuum S/N is below this.  [default: 20.0; x>=0.0]
* `--noise-products / --no-noise-products`: Where self-calibration was applied, also image what it removed and keep it: wsclean[-cube]-selfcal-correction.fits, wsclean[-cube]-residual-total.fits (residual + correction: all the data the model does not explain) and the gain tables in selfcal_gains/ (default).  [default: noise-products]
* `--pbcor / --no-pbcor`: Also primary-beam correct the continuum image and the image cube: wsclean[-cube]-pb.fits (the beam, CASA's ALMA Airy model, per channel) and wsclean[-cube]-image.pbcor.fits (blanked below 0.2). Off by default; 'image pb-correct' adds them to an existing run.  [default: no-pbcor]
* `--casa-data-root <path>`: CASA runtime data for --selfcal (default <output>/.casa-data, downloaded once by the driver when missing, as the calibration stage does).
* `--uv-contsub / --no-uv-contsub`: Subtract the continuum from the visibilities before imaging (CASA uvcontsub): line channels are found on the source spectrum, the continuum is fitted per visibility over the others. The continuum image is made from the fitted continuum and every cube product holds only the lines. Needs --cube and --single-window-ms; replaces --contsub.  [default: no-uv-contsub]
* `--contsub-order <int range>`: Continuum polynomial order for --contsub and --uv-contsub: 0 (constant) or 1 (linear, default).  [default: 1; 0<=x<=1]
* `--spectral-sampling <float range>`: Cube channels per spectral resolution element (the spectral counterpart of --beam-sampling). 2 keeps the native channels of ALMA's Hanning-smoothed windows; 1 halves them.  [default: 2.0; x>=1e-06]
* `--velocity-resolution <float range>`: Narrowest cube channel in km/s at the window's reference frequency (0: no limit).  [default: 0.0; x>=0.0]
* `--max-cube-gb <float range>`: Largest cube per product in GB (32-bit pixels): windows imaged on large grids get fewer, wider channels. Channel counts are divisors of the native count, so every cube channel averages the same number of native channels.  [default: 4.0; x>=0.001]
* `--cube-products <str>`: Comma-separated cube products to keep: image, residual, psf, model, dirty (default: all five). The others are removed (dirty is not even made).  [default: image,residual,psf,model,dirty]
* `--join-channels / --no-join-channels`: Clean the cube on the sum of its channels (WSClean -join-channels): continuum too faint to clean channel by channel is cleaned too, but narrow lines are cleaned worse. Off by default. Needs --cube.  [default: no-join-channels]
* `--cube-line-mask / --no-cube-line-mask`: Clean the cube a second time (-continue) inside the moment-0 mask of the first pass: a line's faint parts, below each channel's own auto-mask but clear in the sum, are cleaned too (default; with --cube and --single-window-ms; ~2x the cube time).  [default: cube-line-mask]
* `--cube-reorder / --cube-no-reorder`: Let WSClean reorder the single-window MS per channel for the cube (default). Without it WSClean re-reads the whole MS for every cube channel: ~25x slower.  [default: cube-reorder]
* `--plan-only`: Print the channel plan and the projected cube volume, then exit without imaging.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim image clean-quality`

Measure how much source signal the clean left in the residuals, task by task.

For every task under OUTPUT_ROOT writes quality.json (continuum and cube
statistics: S/N, the residual's share and profile at the source, the
noise WSClean measured when it built its mask, line and line-free
residuals, model fluxes) and, for cubes, moment maps of the line and of
the residual; prints one row per task and writes them to a CSV. See
almasim.services.imaging.quality for each statistic.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim image clean-quality [OPTIONS] {output_root}
```

**Arguments**:

* `output_root`: An image-from-ms output directory (or one task directory) to assess.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--moments / --no-moments`: Write the cube moment maps (quality/cube-*.fits) next to each task's images.  [default: moments]
* `--summary <path>`: Summary CSV path (default <output_root>/clean-quality.csv).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim image pb-correct`

Primary-beam correct the images of an existing image-from-ms run.

For every row of IMAGING_PARAMETERS whose task finished (a .done marker)
writes wsclean[-cube]-pb.fits and wsclean[-cube]-image.pbcor.fits next to
its continuum image and image cube, as image-from-ms --pbcor does, without
imaging again. The dish diameter comes from the row's fov_per_frequency.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim image pb-correct [OPTIONS] {imaging_parameters} {output_directory}
```

**Arguments**:

* `imaging_parameters`: Parameter CSV the outputs were imaged from  [required]
* `output_directory`: The image-from-ms output directory  [required]

**Options**:

* `--cutoff <float range>`: Blank the corrected images where the beam's response is below this.  [default: 0.2; 0.001<=x<=0.999]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim preview`

Previews of products, written as FITS (moment-style maps, Wiener reconstructions).

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim preview [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `integrate`: Integrate a cube along its spectral axis...
* `wiener`: Reconstruct a simulated observation from...

### `almasim preview integrate`

Integrate a cube along its spectral axis into one image.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim preview integrate [OPTIONS] {product} {output}
```

**Arguments**:

* `product`: A cube to integrate: FITS, NPZ, or a MeasurementSet (gridded first).  [required]
* `output`: The 2D FITS image to write.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--method <sum|mean>`: Sum (moment-0 style) or mean along the axis.  [default: sum]
* `--channel-start <int range>`: First channel to include (default: all).  [x>=0]
* `--channel-end <int range>`: Last channel to include (default: all).  [x>=0]
* `--complex-part <real|imag|magnitude|phase>`: For visibility cubes: the part to show.  [default: real]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim preview wiener`

Reconstruct a simulated observation from its dirty and beam cubes (Wiener filter).

Writes wiener-model.fits, wiener-restored.fits (the model convolved with a
clean beam fitted to each channel's PSF, plus the residual) and
wiener-residual.fits. A quick look, not the reference imaging: that is
WSClean on the simulated MeasurementSet.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim preview wiener [OPTIONS] {dirty} {beam} {output_dir}
```

**Arguments**:

* `dirty`: The dirty cube (FITS or NPZ).  [required]
* `beam`: The beam (PSF) cube, the dirty cube's shape.  [required]
* `output_dir`: Folder for the model, restored and residual.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--epsilon <float range>`: Wiener regularisation (noise-to-signal power).  [default: 0.001; x>=1e-12]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim noise`

Noise models: released versions, components, schema; measuring real data's noise.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `show`: List the released noise models, or show one.
* `components`: The components a noise model can hold, and...
* `schema`: The JSON Schema of a noise model file.
* `windows`: Write the windows table (windows.csv) and...
* `extract`: Measure real windows' noise: the level...
* `fit`: Fit real windows' calibration residuals...
* `aggregate`: Reduce the windows' measurements into a...
* `validate`: Simulate the real windows with a noise...
* `compare`: Compare the windows noise validate...
* `promote`: Write a validated candidate as the next...

### `almasim noise show`

List the released noise models, or show one.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise show [OPTIONS] [model]
```

**Arguments**:

* `model`: A released model ('alma', 'alma@1'), or a JSON file; omitted: list the released models.

**Options**:

* `--noise-only <str>`: Show the model with only these components (comma-separated).
* `--noise-without <str>`: Show the model without these components (comma-separated).
* `--json`: Print the model's JSON.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise components`

The components a noise model can hold, and their parameters.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise components [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise schema`

The JSON Schema of a noise model file.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise schema [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `-o, --output <path>`: Write it here (default: print).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise windows`

Write the windows table (windows.csv) and archive rows (rows.csv) of an
imaging run, for noise extract, fit and validate. A 7 m array's windows have
no PWV: its antennas carry no water vapour radiometer.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise windows [OPTIONS] {parameters}
```

**Arguments**:

* `parameters`: The imaging run's parameters CSV (image compute-parameters').  [required]

**Options**:

* `--images <directory>`: The imaging run's output folder (image image-from-ms').  [required]
* `--metadata <file>`: The archive search the data came from (an almasim metadata CSV).  [required]
* `--products <file>`: Resolved-products CSV(s) of those observations, which link each MS's execution block to its observation (default: *products*.csv beside --metadata).
* `--out <path>`: Where windows.csv and rows.csv go.  [required]
* `--done-only / --all-tasks`: Only windows whose imaging task finished (its .done marker) and was assessed (image clean-quality's quality.json, which fit and validate read).  [default: done-only]
* `--science-only / --all-fields`: Only science target fields (OBSERVE_TARGET), read from each MS.  [default: science-only]
* `--max-windows <int range>`: Keep the first N windows.  [x>=1]
* `--names <str>`: Only these windows (comma-separated names, as a previous run listed them).
* `--qa0-report-root <directory>`: Root of the extracted auxiliary deliveries (<project>/science_goal.*/group.*/member.*/qa/): each window's PWV is its execution block's, from its QA0 report (default: the archive row's, which is one block's of the observing unit).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise extract`

Measure real windows' noise: the level against WEIGHT, the channel
correlation, ALMA's Tsys across the window, one visibility's noise and
each antenna's noise shape (window.json).

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise extract [OPTIONS] [ms]
```

**Arguments**:

* `ms`: A calibrated MeasurementSet (*.ms.split.cal); or give --windows.

**Options**:

* `--out <path>`: Where the measurements go (windows/<name>/).  [required]
* `--spw <int range>`: The MS's spectral window.  [x>=0]
* `--field <str>`: Field name or id (default: every field).
* `--name <str>`: The window's name (default: uid, spw, field).
* `--syscal-ms <path>`: Where to read SYSCAL's Tsys (default: the MS).
* `--line-channels <str>`: Channels of line emission to leave out ('a~b;c').
* `--task-log <path>`: An ALMASim imaging task's log; its 'lines in channels' are left out.
* `--pwv <float range>`: The window's precipitable water vapour (mm; its execution block's), for noise aggregate's receiver temperatures and noise validate.  [x>=0]
* `--windows <path>`: A CSV of windows (columns ms, spw; optional field, name, pwv, syscal_ms, line_channels, task_log), measured one per task.
* `--max-visibilities <int range>`: Rows are sampled evenly over the observation up to about this many visibilities.  [default: 40000000; x>=1000]
* `--overwrite`: Measure windows again even when measured.
* `--allow-partial`: Succeed when some windows fail and at least one did not (failures stay listed).
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 02:00:00]
* `--slurm-cores <int range>`: Cores per Slurm worker.  [default: 2; x>=1]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 32GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Slurm workers measuring windows at once.  [default: 4; x>=1]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--scheduler-interface <str>`: Scheduler/worker network interface (e.g. ib0, eth0).
* `--task-timeout <float range>`: Timeout in seconds for each worker-side command.  [default: 14400.0; x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise fit`

Fit real windows' calibration residuals against their clean models: the
slow and fast atmospheric phase, the antenna gains' and the baselines' own
errors (fit.json), the values of the noise model's slow_phase, fast_phase,
antenna_gains and baseline_errors components.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise fit [OPTIONS] [ms]
```

**Arguments**:

* `ms`: A calibrated MeasurementSet (*.ms.split.cal); or give --windows.

**Options**:

* `--out <path>`: The noise extract output (windows/<name>/window.json); fit.json goes beside it.  [required]
* `--spw <int range>`: The MS's spectral window.  [x>=0]
* `--field <str>`: Field name or id (default: every field).
* `--name <str>`: The window's name, as noise extract gave it.
* `--task-dir <path>`: The window's ALMASim imaging task (its clean models and quality.json).
* `--windows <path>`: A CSV of windows, as for noise extract, with a task_dir column.
* `--continuum-model <str>`: The continuum clean model: 'masked' (where the image is above 5 sigma) or 'all'.  [default: masked]
* `--line-model <str>`: The cube clean model: 'masked' (line channels, inside the line mask), 'all' or 'none'.  [default: masked]
* `--realizations <int range>`: Draws of the noise-only references.  [default: 3; x>=1]
* `--seed <int>`: Seed of the references' draws.  [default: 0]
* `--overwrite`: Fit windows again even when fitted.
* `--allow-partial`: Succeed when some windows fail and at least one did not (failures stay listed).
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 04:00:00]
* `--slurm-cores <int range>`: Cores per Slurm worker.  [default: 4; x>=1]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 64GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Slurm workers fitting windows at once.  [default: 4; x>=1]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--scheduler-interface <str>`: Scheduler/worker network interface (e.g. ib0, eth0).
* `--task-timeout <float range>`: Timeout in seconds for each worker-side command.  [default: 28800.0; x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise aggregate`

Reduce the windows' measurements into a candidate noise model: each value
they measure is their median, with its window count and spread recorded.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise aggregate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--out <path>`: The noise extract and fit output (windows/<name>/window.json, fit.json).  [required]
* `--from <str>`: The model whose values the windows' replace ('alma', 'alma@1' or a file).  [default: alma]
* `--output <path>`: Where the candidate goes (default: <out>/candidate.json).
* `--name <str>`: The candidate's name (default: <base>-candidate).
* `--version <int range>`: The candidate's version (default: the base's + 1).  [x>=1]
* `--min-windows <int range>`: Windows a value needs; fewer keep the base's.  [default: 3; x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise validate`

Simulate the real windows with a noise model, measure and image them as
the real ones were, and compare (validation/<model sha>/comparison.json).

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise validate [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--model <str>`: The model to validate: a candidate file or a released name.  [required]
* `--windows <path>`: The windows table noise extract measured (name, ms, spw; task_dir: their imaging).  [required]
* `--metadata <path>`: Each window's archive row (as 'almasim metadata' writes them) with a name column.  [required]
* `--measured <path>`: noise extract's output for the real windows.  [required]
* `--out <path>`: Where the validation goes (validation/<model sha>/).  [required]
* `--name <str>`: Validate only this window of the table.
* `--seed <int>`: The simulations' seed (per window, plus its name's).  [default: 0]
* `--keep-ms`: Keep the simulated MSs.
* `--wsclean-bin <str>`
* `--casa-data-root <str>`
* `--num-cores <int range>`: [default: 8; x>=1]
* `--task-memory-gb <float range>`: [default: 40.0; x>=1.0]
* `--imaging-timeout <float range>`: [default: 10800.0; x>=60]
* `--criteria <path>`: A JSON file of comparison criteria (noise compare's).
* `--overwrite`: Validate windows again.
* `--allow-partial`: Succeed when some windows fail and at least one did not (failures stay listed).
* `--judge / --no-judge`: Compare the validated windows at the end.  [default: judge]
* `--backend, --postprocess-backend <sync|slurm>`: Where the tasks run: sync (this process, one at a time) or slurm (Slurm jobs).  [default: sync]
* `--slurm-queue <str>`: Slurm queue/partition.  [default: normal]
* `--slurm-project <str>`: Slurm project/account.
* `--slurm-walltime <str>`: Slurm walltime per worker job (HH:MM:SS).  [default: 08:00:00]
* `--slurm-memory <str>`: Memory per Slurm worker.  [default: 64GB]
* `--slurm-workers <int range>`: Slurm workers validating windows at once.  [default: 4; x>=1]
* `--scheduler-host, --slurm-scheduler-host <str>`: Scheduler host advertised to the workers (default: this host).
* `--scheduler-interface <str>`: Scheduler/worker network interface (e.g. ib0, eth0).
* `--task-timeout <float range>`: Timeout in seconds for each worker-side command.  [default: 43200.0; x>=1]
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise compare`

Compare the windows noise validate simulated with the real ones
(comparison.json): per metric the median ratio or difference, its range,
Wilcoxon p, and whether the model passes the criteria.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise compare [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--model <str>`: The model validated.  [required]
* `--windows <path>`: The windows table.  [required]
* `--measured <path>`: noise extract's output for the real windows.  [required]
* `--out <path>`: noise validate's output.  [required]
* `--criteria <path>`: A JSON file of comparison criteria.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim noise promote`

Write a validated candidate as the next version of a released model
(models/<name>-<n+1>.json), refused unless its comparison passed. The pull
request that adds the file, and with it moves the model to the new
version, stays with a person. With --site it goes to the site's models
folder instead, under a name of its own, recording who released it.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim noise promote [OPTIONS] {candidate}
```

**Arguments**:

* `candidate`: The candidate model (noise aggregate's, or any file).  [required]

**Options**:

* `--comparison <path>`: noise validate's comparison.json of that very model.  [required]
* `--name <str>`: The model it releases (default: the candidate's, less -candidate).
* `--models-dir <path>`: Where released models live (default: this checkout's).
* `--site`: Release into the site's models folder (ALMASIM_NOISE_MODELS, else the profile's [tools] noise_models), where simulations find it at once.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim jobs`

List, follow and control runs submitted with `almasim submit` or the web console.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

* `list`: List runs, newest first.
* `show`: Show one run: its command, resources,...
* `logs`: Print a run's output.
* `cancel`: Stop a run (yours only).
* `delete`: Remove a finished run's folder (yours...
* `resubmit`: Run the same command again, with the same...

### `almasim jobs list`

List runs, newest first.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--all`: Include the team's runs, not only yours.
* `--limit <int range>`: How many runs to show, newest first.  [default: 20; x>=1]
* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim jobs show`

Show one run: its command, resources, state and files.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs show [OPTIONS] {run_id}
```

**Arguments**:

* `run_id`: Run id, or its first or last characters.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim jobs logs`

Print a run's output.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs logs [OPTIONS] {run_id}
```

**Arguments**:

* `run_id`: Run id, or its first or last characters.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--stderr`: Show stderr.log instead of stdout.log.
* `-f, --follow`: Keep printing until the run ends.
* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim jobs cancel`

Stop a run (yours only).

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs cancel [OPTIONS] {run_id}
```

**Arguments**:

* `run_id`: Run id, or its first or last characters.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim jobs delete`

Remove a finished run's folder (yours only); outputs written elsewhere stay.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs delete [OPTIONS] {run_id}
```

**Arguments**:

* `run_id`: Run id, or its first or last characters.  [required]

**Options**:

* `-y, --yes`: Do not ask first.
* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `almasim jobs resubmit`

Run the same command again, with the same resources, as a new run.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim jobs resubmit [OPTIONS] {run_id}
```

**Arguments**:

* `run_id`: Run id, or its first or last characters.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE or ~/.config/almasim).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim clean`

Run WSClean and forward all extra arguments unchanged.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim clean [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--wsclean-bin <str>`: Path or executable name for WSClean binary.  [default: wsclean]
* `--cwd <path>`: Optional working directory for WSClean execution.
* `--dry-run`: Print the WSClean command without running it.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim doctor`

Check the runs root, Python, CASA, WSClean and Slurm the profile names.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim doctor [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--slurm`: Run the checks on a compute node (with srun), as a job sees them.
* `--site-profile <path>`: Site profile (default: $ALMASIM_SITE_PROFILE).
* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE, else ~/.config/almasim/almasim.toml).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim update-shared`

Rebuild the shared install from ``ref`` with the recorded repo and template.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim update-shared [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--ref <str>`: Branch, tag or commit to install.  [default: main]
* `--prefix <path>`: The install (default: the one this almasim runs from).
* `--repo <str>`: Git URL to clone (default: the one the install recorded).
* `--template <str>`: Site profile template, relative to the repo (default: the recorded one).
* `--force`: Update even while runs are not finished (they may break).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim submit`

Submit ``almasim <command>`` with the profile's defaults and these overrides.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim submit [OPTIONS] {command}...
```

**Arguments**:

* `command...`: The almasim command line to run.  [required]

**Options**:

* `--partition <str>`: Slurm partition.
* `--account <str>`: Slurm account.
* `--cpus <int range>`: CPUs for the job.  [x>=1]
* `--memory <str>`: Memory for the job, e.g. 16G.
* `--time <str>`: Time limit, e.g. 02:00:00 or 2-00:00:00.
* `--title <str>`: A name for the run.
* `--after <str>`: Start only when this run has succeeded (its id). Repeatable.
* `--wait`: Wait for the run to end; exit 1 unless it succeeded.
* `--profile <path>`: User profile (default: $ALMASIM_PROFILE, else ~/.config/almasim/almasim.toml).
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## `almasim serve`

Serve the console; print the ssh tunnel line and the link with its access token.

**Usage**:

```console
$ almasim serve [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

* `--port <int range>`: Listen on 127.0.0.1:<port> instead of a private socket in ~/.almasim (in a container, ALMASIM_SERVE_HOST sets the address).  [1024<=x<=65535]
* `--base-path <str>`: Serve under this URL prefix, for a reverse proxy that passes it on (Open OnDemand's /node/<host>/<port>).  [env var: ALMASIM_BASE_PATH]
* `--managed`: Started and stopped by a portal (Open OnDemand): needs --port and keeps no record in ~/.almasim, so --status and --stop do not see it.
* `--status`: Show the running console's link.
* `--stop`: Stop the running console.
* `--help`: Show this message and exit.
